data.turoyo: Aṯi, amṭele i čaqane lu šexayḏe. ʕAṣriye yatu, ḥəfle eba, latwaybe kewo, səmwayleyo, ḥəǧǧa simowayle, nayəḥle.
data.translation: Er kam nach Hause und brachte seinem Scheich die Schale. Der setzte sich abends hin und wusch sich daraus. Er hatte ja gar keine Krankheit; es war nur ein Vorwand, den er gebraucht hatte. Nun wurde er (natürlich) gesund.

rationale: Completes Preterit to five and records objectless bathing with instrumental eba; the bowl is explicit in the retained opening sentence.

summary: The corpus supports the inherited single sense Waschen (ambitransitive). Human self-bathing can lack ruḥ-; washing another person has a patient NP or l-series object suffix. Neither configuration needs a new numbered sense.

The alternation is visible inside individual verses: 88/253 contrasts “which of us washes first?” with “I wash you”; MAC Xalaf Agha/20 contrasts objectless ḥuf with koḥayfole. Transitivity does not require a different stem or a Detransitive section.

Preterit with L-series agents occurs in both self-directed and transitive washing. Ḥə́flali is a useful female-agent/first-person-patient combination. Instrumental b- with a bowl contrasts with locative b- at a bath.
Infectum-wa documents customary bathing and a recurring abstention from bathing until Epiphany. The negative lo+ḥayfìwayna has not been reclassified as a different sense.
Animal washing is already illustrated in the inherited donkey example; the mare at 78/81 is a participant extension within the same washing sense, rather than a new lexical use.
No lexicalized light-verb or noun collocation is demonstrated. Coordination with šyġ and bath-going provides context for valency; it does not warrant an Idiomatic phrases addition.
